item.title: G8 Education receives takeover approach from Majority Capital Partners
item.description: ASX listed early childhood education and care provider (ECEC) G8 Education has received a non-binding, indicative proposal from Australian private equity firm Majority Capital Partners in a deal that values the business at around $196 million.

item.title: Victorian Liberals and Nationals commit to retaining Free Kinder and reviewing early learning
item.description: The Victorian Liberals and Nationals would maintain Free Kinder and review the early learning sector focusing on funding, regulation, compliance, infrastructure, capacity and workforce if elected, Shadow Minister for Education Brad Rowswell told a sector forum.

item.title: NSW Liberals and Nationals pledge to restore Start Strong preschool funding
item.description: The NSW Liberals and Nationals have committed to returning funding for the Start Strong program for community preschools, plus funding for preschool programs for approved long day care services if elected.

item.title: New report on rural meal provision gap prompts call for targeted early learning funding
item.description: A new national report has called for targeted investment in food provision across early learning services with findings revealing only 58% of long day care services in small rural towns provided meals, including lunch, compared to 91% nationally.

item.title: First Nations languages in early learning: starting with people, not a word list
item.description: When considering introducing local First Nations language into your early learning program, knowing where to begin can feel uncertain. Community Early Learning Australia’s (CELA) guidance explores how educators can approach this respectfully, starting with relationships, permission and advice from the community whose language they hope to share.

item.title: Teachers are being prepared to enter the profession. But are they being prepared to stay?
item.description: Teachers are being prepared to enter the teaching profession however they may not be being adequately prepared to stay in the profession. A new report by the University of Melbourne highlights that teachers’ well-being is one of the biggest factors influencing their staying power. However, it is not currently being taught as a part of teacher training programs. Future teachers are expected to manage increasingly complex classrooms, student mental health, family relationships and increased worklo
